summary: Murray Field (EKA/KEKA) is a county-owned general aviation airport serving Eureka and California's Humboldt County, located about two miles north of downtown near Humboldt Bay. It has two short asphalt runways and supports private, flight-training, and emergency aircraft rather than scheduled airline service. It is a convenient local alternative to California Redwood Coast-Humboldt County Airport (ACV) for general aviation traffic.
faqs:
Q: Does Murray Field have commercial airline service?
A: No. Murray Field is a general aviation airport; scheduled passenger flights operate from California Redwood Coast-Humboldt County Airport (ACV), about 15 miles north.

Q: What runways are at EKA?
A: Murray Field has two asphalt runways, 12/30 and 16/34, each roughly 3,000 feet long, with pilot-controlled lighting.

Q: How far is Murray Field from downtown Eureka?
A: It is roughly 2-3 miles north of downtown Eureka, typically a 5-10 minute drive via US 101 and Murray Road.

Q: Is fuel available at Murray Field?
A: Yes, self-serve 100LL avgas is typically available, along with tiedown and transient parking; check current fees and after-hours access with Humboldt County.
transport_tips: Murray Field is easiest to reach by car: from US 101, take the Murray Road exit and follow airport signs west toward Humboldt Bay. Taxi and rideshare service can be limited, especially early or late, so arrange a pickup in advance. There is no direct public transit to the airport area, but downtown Eureka is only a short drive away; allow extra time in coastal fog.
local_tip: Frequent visitors check the AWOS and marine-layer trends before departing: EKA can be fogged in while ACV or inland areas are clear, especially on summer mornings.
